newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS expects to remove cargo fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: SAS expects to remove cargo fuel surcharge.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS said on Friday it expected to follow other airlines and remove a fuel surcharge on air cargo.
"We will in the next few days take a decision that will be in line with what the other airlines have decided," SAS spokesman Knut Lovstuhagen told Reuters.
"But we will make our own decision, based on our situation," he added.
SAS introduced a surcharge of 10 cents a kilo on intercontinental flights and five cents a kilo on European fligths in November last year, in response to surging jet fuel prices.
But jet fuel prices have fallen and last week the airline said it would drop the surcharge if prices kept decreasing.

KLM and Swisscargo said earlier on Friday they would drop fuel surcharges on cargo as of April 15 and Cathay Pacific said its surcharges on flights from Britain the UK will be removed effective May 1.
On Thursday, Lufthansa, the world's largest international freight carrier, said it was scrapping fuel surcharges effective April 15.
